Every door, window, rear-porch door and chandelier cell in joinery is therefore locked. The only cells joinery can reach are the shutters, which sit on the gallery and porch side of the wall. I'll remove the refused writes in joinery.mjs and rerun make.sh.

input.summary:
parts/joinery.mjs now places only the 260 shutters (open dark-oak trapdoors) flat on the wall beside every opening; make.sh's joinery line shows no REFUSED and no OFF-PALETTE, and build.nbt is written.
The doors, windows, rear-porch door and hall chandeliers are removed from this part, because the shell carves those cells to air and runParts locks them.
The original file is kept at /tmp/joinery.orig.mjs so the calls can go back once the shell stops claiming the openings.
left: The part is not built as specified: no fanlit front doors (both floors), no tall windows or sidelights and transoms (front, ends, south, rear wing), no garden/service doors, no rear-porch door (x47..48 z75), no hall chandeliers. Every one of those cells is shell-owned air, so runParts refuses it (546 refused writes before the fix).
Shutters now stand flat on solid white wall with no window behind them on the front, end and south faces. They read as decoration of blank walls until the openings are filled.

The real fix is outside this part and needs a decision: parts/shell.mjs must leave the opening cells unplaced instead of carving them to air (the box fill and open() calls for the windows, doors, rear-porch door and hall air), or runParts must let a later part fill air that an earlier part only carved. After that, restore the calls from /tmp/joinery.orig.mjs.

Out of scope for this part, seen in the same make.sh run: roof.json lays OFF-PALETTE blocks (tuff_bricks, tuff_brick_slab, tuff_brick_stairs, cobbled_deepslate_stairs/slab, polished_deepslate_slab/stairs, stone_brick_slab) for the roof part to fix.

waste.what: Traced which of the 546 refusals came from which call by reading runParts' write() and the shell's open() calls, and then checked by hand that the windows, doors and chandeliers were all shell-owned air.
waste.cost: About 6 source reads plus one full make.sh run; the report only keeps the first 8 refused cells, so the count could not be attributed to calls.
waste.tool: runParts should group refusals by the helper call or cell range that made them and name the owning part (for example 'shell open() 45..50 y4..9 z42'). A `ownedBy(view, x, y, z)` query would let a part check before it writes.

waste.what: Rewrote parts/joinery.mjs by hand to remove every opening call (about 25 call sites) and the helpers and imports they left unused.
waste.cost: One full-file rewrite of about 40 lines, plus two make.sh runs.
waste.tool: A plan-level OPENINGS owner table (or a shell option that leaves opening cells unplaced) would let the shell and the joinery split the openings without a lock conflict; the joinery part would then need no rewrite.

companions.task: Hang the fanlit double front doors on both floors, the garden and service doors and the rear-porch door, with their posts, transoms and lintels, once the shell leaves those openings unplaced.
Fit the tall sash windows, sidelights and transoms, with their sills and lintels, into every opening on the front, ends, south face and rear wing.

structured_output.summary:
parts/joinery.mjs now places only the 260 shutters (open dark-oak trapdoors) flat on the wall beside every opening; make.sh's joinery line shows no REFUSED and no OFF-PALETTE, and build.nbt is written.
The doors, windows, rear-porch door and hall chandeliers are removed from this part, because the shell carves those cells to air and runParts locks them.
The original file is kept at /tmp/joinery.orig.mjs so the calls can go back once the shell stops claiming the openings.
left: The part is not built as specified: no fanlit front doors (both floors), no tall windows or sidelights and transoms (front, ends, south, rear wing), no garden/service doors, no rear-porch door (x47..48 z75), no hall chandeliers. Every one of those cells is shell-owned air, so runParts refuses it (546 refused writes before the fix).
Shutters now stand flat on solid white wall with no window behind them on the front, end and south faces. They read as decoration of blank walls until the openings are filled.

The real fix is outside this part and needs a decision: parts/shell.mjs must leave the opening cells unplaced instead of carving them to air (the box fill and open() calls for the windows, doors, rear-porch door and hall air), or runParts must let a later part fill air that an earlier part only carved. After that, restore the calls from /tmp/joinery.orig.mjs.

Out of scope for this part, seen in the same make.sh run: roof.json lays OFF-PALETTE blocks (tuff_bricks, tuff_brick_slab, tuff_brick_stairs, cobbled_deepslate_stairs/slab, polished_deepslate_slab/stairs, stone_brick_slab) for the roof part to fix.

waste.what: Traced which of the 546 refusals came from which call by reading runParts' write() and the shell's open() calls, and then checked by hand that the windows, doors and chandeliers were all shell-owned air.
waste.cost: About 6 source reads plus one full make.sh run; the report only keeps the first 8 refused cells, so the count could not be attributed to calls.
waste.tool: runParts should group refusals by the helper call or cell range that made them and name the owning part (for example 'shell open() 45..50 y4..9 z42'). A `ownedBy(view, x, y, z)` query would let a part check before it writes.

waste.what: Rewrote parts/joinery.mjs by hand to remove every opening call (about 25 call sites) and the helpers and imports they left unused.
waste.cost: One full-file rewrite of about 40 lines, plus two make.sh runs.
waste.tool: A plan-level OPENINGS owner table (or a shell option that leaves opening cells unplaced) would let the shell and the joinery split the openings without a lock conflict; the joinery part would then need no rewrite.

companions.task: Hang the fanlit double front doors on both floors, the garden and service doors and the rear-porch door, with their posts, transoms and lintels, once the shell leaves those openings unplaced.
Fit the tall sash windows, sidelights and transoms, with their sills and lintels, into every opening on the front, ends, south face and rear wing.
